root_cause.text: The cleanup loop uses post-decrement (`while(i--)`) which skips the current failing index i before processing it, causing the device at index i to not be cleaned up when a failure occurs during initialization.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes the cleanup loop from `while(i--)` to `do { ... } while(i--)`, ensuring the failing index i is processed before decrementing. Additionally, the patch adds `i--` in the devlink_alloc failure path to adjust i to point to the last successfully allocated index, preventing the loop from attempting to clean up an uninitialized device. The CVE description explicitly states: "The current cleanup loop while(i--) skip the failing index i, causing a memory leak."

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix off-by-one error in device cleanup by decrementing loop counter before error exit to prevent processing uninitialized device.
intent_record.what: Added `i--;` statement before the `goto setup_nic_dev_free;` label in the devlink allocation failure path of the setup_nic_devices function.
intent_record.how: When devlink allocation fails, the code jumps to the cleanup label. Without decrementing `i`, the cleanup loop would attempt to process one extra device that was never successfully initialized. Decrementing `i` ensures the cleanup only processes devices that were actually set up, preventing out-of-bounds access or double-free issues in the error handling path.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix off-by-one error in NIC device cleanup loop to ensure all allocated devices are properly destroyed on setup failure.
intent_record.what: Changed the error cleanup loop from a while(i--) pre-decrement loop to a do-while(i--) post-decrement loop structure.
intent_record.how: This ensures the cleanup loop executes at least once even if i is 0 at entry, processing the device at index 0 before decrementing. The original while(i--) would skip the final iteration when i reaches 0, leaving the device at index 0 uncleanup if an error occurred during its setup.

candidates.rationale: The post-decrement operator (i--) in the while condition decrements i before the loop body executes, causing the loop to skip processing the device at the current index i when a failure occurs. This means the device at the failing index is never cleaned up. The fix should use pre-decrement (--i) or decrement before the loop to ensure all allocated devices from index 0 to i-1 are properly destroyed.

vuln_statements.explanation: The post-decrement operator (i--) in the while condition causes the loop to skip the device at the current failing index i before processing it in the cleanup loop body. When a failure occurs during initialization at index i, the post-decrement evaluates the condition with the current value of i, then decrements it before entering the loop body. This means the device at index i is never cleaned up. The vulnerable statement should use pre-decrement (--i) or decrement i before the loop to ensure all allocated devices from index 0 through the failing index are properly destroyed.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable code is present in the `setup_nic_devices` function at the cleanup label `setup_nic_dev_fail:`. The cleanup loop uses `while (i--)` which is a post-decrement operation. This means when a failure occurs at index `i`, the loop decrements `i` first before processing it, causing the device at the failing index to be skipped. Specifically, the code shows: `while (i--) { dev_err(...); liquidio_destroy_nic_device(octeon_dev, i); }`. If setup fails at interface index 2 (i=2), the loop will decrement to i=1 and process that, skipping the cleanup of the device at index 2 that actually failed. The fix would require using pre-decrement `while (--i)` or restructuring the loop to handle the current index before decrementing.
